title: Rethinking the production and publication of machine-readable expressions of research findings
abstract: Scientific literature is the primary expression of scientific knowledge and an important source of research data. However, scientific knowledge expressed in narrative text documents is not inherently machine readable. To facilitate knowledge reuse, knowledge must be extracted from articles and organized into databases post-publication. The high time costs and inaccuracies associated with completing these activities manually has driven the development of techniques that automate knowledge extraction. Tackling the problem with a different mindset, we propose a pre-publication approach, known as reborn, that ensures scientific knowledge is born readable, i.e. produced in a machine-readable format with formal data syntax during knowledge production. We implement the approach using the Open Research Knowledge Graph infrastructure for FAIR scientific knowledge organization. With a focus on statistical research findings, we test the approach with three use cases in soil science, computer science, and agroecology. Our results suggest that the proposed approach is superior compared to classical manual and semi-automated post-publication extraction techniques in terms of knowledge accuracy, richness, and reproducibility as well as technological simplicity.
notes: Full-paper extraction covering Introduction, Results (three use cases), Discussion (Comparing approaches, Impact, Limitations), and Methods. The manuscript is methodological/infrastructural rather than empirical biological; assertions are largely conceptual/methodological with three use-case applications used as supporting evidence.

A quick analysis of approximately 90K Zenodo records showed that about 5K (~5%) contain either Python or R files and are interlinked (in metadata) to about 8K published articles. While 8K articles are a very small fraction of the millions of articles published each year⁵⁸, the Zenodo data does suggest that in the course of a few years, hundreds, and in the longer run thousands, of articles could be interlinked with machine-readable expressions of the research findings published therein, an important impact and impulse for the future of digital scholarship and the efficient reuse of scientific knowledge as FAIR research data.

qa_items.question_text: What is the evidence status for the claim: "The reborn approach is superior to classical manual and semi-automated post-publication extraction in terms of knowledge accuracy, richness, reproducibility, and technological simplicity."?
What evidence supports the claim: "The reborn approach was applied to three use cases and produced machine-readable research findings in each, demonstrating practical viability."?

answers.answer_text: Three use-case deployments are reported: soil science (Gentsch et al., reborn data 10.48366/R664252), computer science (Thießen et al., reborn data 10.48366/R661500), and agroecology (Perez-Alvarez et al., reborn data 10.48366/R689181).

qa_items.question_text: What limitations or flaws could weaken the claim: "The reborn approach is superior to classical manual and semi-automated post-publication extraction."?

answers.answer_text: Three author-stated limitations apply: (a) scope is currently restricted to quantitative/statistical knowledge in R/Python; (b) ORKG templates capture only data syntax (no formal semantics, no reasoning); (c) the system relies on authors to select which findings to express, limiting coverage. The evaluation also only spans three use cases, limiting external validity.

qa_items.question_text: What knowledge gaps remain for the claim: "Pre-publication production may make post-publication extraction largely obsolete in the second half of the century."?

answers.answer_text: Open gaps include: extending reborn to qualitative/formal knowledge types (G0001); adding formal semantics and ontology mappings to support reasoning (G0002); reducing author overhead to support broad adoption (G0003).

qa_items.question_text: Under what biological/research contexts is the claim "The reborn approach is superior to post-publication extraction" evaluated in this paper?

answers.answer_text: The claim is evaluated in three statistical-data-analysis contexts (soil science, computer science, agroecology) implemented in R and Python with ORKG templates, and compared along Accuracy, Richness, Simplicity, Scalability, Coverage, and Legacy.

qa_items.question_text: What mechanism is proposed to deliver superior accuracy and richness compared to post-publication extraction?

answers.answer_text: Embedding expressive data-type schemata (ORKG templates) into the data analysis itself lets the script produce machine-readable expressions of inputs/outputs (e.g. dataset, p-value) directly, avoiding copy/approximation errors and capturing richer structure than post-publication NLP/manual extraction. Listing 1 demonstrates this for a Student's t-test, and the three use cases instantiate it for LMMs, SEM, and TDMS data.
